node.statement: Let B be a finite-dimensional unital C*-algebra. Every nonzero projection p contains a minimal nonzero subprojection: among nonzero projections q<=p choose q minimizing dim(qBq). If qBq were not Cq, it would contain a self-adjoint h not proportional to q. The finite spectrum of h would then have at least two points, and polynomial interpolation on that spectrum would produce a nonzero proper spectral projection r in C*(h) contained in qBq. Thus r<q and rBr is a proper subspace of qBq, contradicting the choice of q. Hence qBq=Cq. By repeatedly choosing such projections, finite dimensionality gives a maximal pairwise orthogonal family p_1,...,p_m of minimal projections. Its sum is 1, since otherwise the nonzero projection 1-sum_i p_i would contain another minimal projection orthogonal to the family. In particular p_i B p_i=C p_i for every i.
